Clarke. These are distinct authority identities. Democracy and Reaction is Hobhouse's book with a later introduction by Peter Clarke, not evidence of a 1904 career.

UWI confirms b's James Robertson earned his BA in 1981 and PhD in 1993, ruling out authorship of the 1908 thesis. Only a's modern Jamaican strand belongs with b.

a is Stanford's American historian Richard White, author of The Middle Ground, The Organic Machine and Railroaded. b is the University of Sydney Australian historian, whose publisher lists Inventing Australia, Australian Travel Writing and On Holidays. The two authority identities describe different people, not duplicate records for one scholar.

The 1997 camp-meeting dissertation is by William Courtland Johnson (UC Riverside), whereas b is William Allen Johnson, the classicist responsible for Bookrolls and Scribes in Oxyrhynchus and Readers and Reading Culture. Their different LC identities correspond to different authors and research careers.

a's Greek-history and oratory articles are by Gunther Martin, including Interpreting Instability (2014), listed on his Bern faculty page. b is Geoffrey Haward Martin (1928-2007), the British municipal historian and archivist responsible for the Ipswich rolls and Domesday translation. The corpus expansion to George H. is misleading.
